headline: Discussed revised Burlington Forward Resolution, youth programs, and an Overdose Prevention Center without final action.
summary: Speakers and councilors discussed the revised Burlington Forward Resolution, including concerns about policing and whether it should be postponed. Discussion also covered the need for an Overdose Prevention Center and for more youth programs. The minutes record no final action on these items.

1. Call to Order 
a. Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson called the meeting to order at 5:35 pm. 
2. Approve Agenda & Minutes 
a. Councilor Grant moved to approve the agenda and adopt the minutes. Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson 
seconded motion. The motion passed unanimously.  
3. Public Forum 
a. Bruce Wilson shared his excitement for the discussions about youth council. He expressed how 
important it is to have youth engaged in conversations. 
b. Ed Baker emphasized the importance of opening an Overdose Prevention Center as soon as possible, 
advocating for a location accessible to people who need services and close to downtown. 
i. Bruce Wilson raised questions about how the OPC would operate and how it might affect drug 
activity in the surrounding area. 
1. Councilor Grant shared there is information on OPCs on the City website. Refer to the 
video. 
c. Andre Clark expressed concerns that the Burlington Forward Resolution disproportionately targets 
unhoused people and people experiencing substance use challenges. He emphasized the need to 
support already-stretched service organizations. He encouraged the City to work collaboratively with 
community organizations and reconsider moving the resolution forward before concerns are addressed. 
d. Councilor Grant discussed the need for coordinated statewide action to address drug trafficking and 
improve public safety. Refer to the video. 
e. Mark Hughes shared concerns about the revised Burlington Forward Resolution, including continued 
authorization for expanded policing without first addressing documented racial disparities in police 
stops, arrests, and use of force. He also expressed concern that recommendations for a dedicated civil 
rights structure within City government had not been adequately addressed. Refer to the video. 
4. Office of REIB Updates 
a. Director Perkins shared updates on ongoing REIB initiatives: 
i. Manager training focused on retention is beginning this month and continuing through 
November.
ii. Registration is being developed for training on what it means to demonstrate equity in the 
workplace. 
iii. The Burlington Aging Council is progressing, including work on a dedicated City webpage with 
resources for older adults. 
iv. REIB is working on relationship repair with the Missisquoi community following the City’s 
decision not to accept a statue gift. 
v. The Community and Belonging Program Manager position has been posted, and community 
members were encouraged to share the opportunity. 
b. Andre Clark offered to support winter supply and giveaway efforts again this year. Kelli noted limited 
staff capacity at the moment and shared she would connect with him. 
5. Supporting & Investing in Burlington’s Youth 
a. Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson presented an overview of the City’s historical youth-focused work and the 
current landscape of services and community partnerships. Refer to the video. 
b. Councilor Grant emphasized the need for more affordable, accessible activities for youth ages 12-18, 
particularly as young people age out of existing camps and programs. 
c. Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson noted that young people, including high school students, have perspectives 
on downtown safety that are not sufficiently represented in City discussions. She highlighted that fewer 
than 5% of respondents to a survey concerning the next police chief were age 30 or younger. 
d. Councilor Grant highlighted the importance of safe, substance-free spaces, including programs and 
events offered by organizations such as Oddfellows and the Community Sailing Center. 
e. Andre Clark emphasized the need for teen centers, multilingual support services, trauma screening and 
support, and opportunities for City leaders to engage directly with students in schools. 
f. Maria Cecilia Hayes suggested that tournaments, group activities, and incentives could help maintain 
youth interest and create opportunities for connection. 
g. Bruce Wilson discussed creating more pathways for youth to access employment and become involved 
in City decision-making. 
h. Liz Clements emphasized that students are interested in advocacy and would benefit from a central City 
contact to help connect them with opportunities. 
i. Ben Traverse noted that the Youth on Boards initiative has lost momentum. Reviving it would require 
dedicated support orientation, and opportunities for youth participants to connect with peers and learn 
about civic engagement. 
j. Mark Hughes emphasized that youth initiatives should be community-driven rather than dictated by City 
leadership. He highlighted the need to reinvest in marginalized communities and support locally 
developed initiatives. 
k. Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson will contact additional youth-serving organizations and convene youth 
groups to gather direct feedback. The committee will continue exploring a citywide assessment of youth 
needs, existing resources, and potential investments. Refer to the video 
6. Updates & Next Steps on Burlington Forward 
a. Councilor Traverse reviewed the revised Burlington Forward Resolution and explained that the intention 
is to bring it to City Council on October 26, 2026, to consider replacing the original resolution with the 
revised version and determining the next steps for further review. Refer to the video. 
i. Andre Clark raised concerns about the proposed public safety response teams, increased 
penalties for low-level drug trafficking, and language. He also emphasized the importance of 
preserving public restrooms and addressing gaps in supportive services. 
ii. Mark Hughes stated that concerns raised by the Vermont Racial Justice Alliance were not fully 
reflected in the revised resolution. He reiterated that expanses policing should not move 
forward without addressing racial disparities in police interactions and strengthening civil rights 
oversight.
iii. Councilor Grant expressed frustration with the process for reviewing and revising the resolution. 
Refer to the video. 
iv. Chris McGrath discussed whether the resolution should be postponed to allow more time for 
review. Refer to the video 
v. Ed Baker emphasized the urgency of opening the Overdose Prevention Center, citing overdose 
deaths and the need to avoid further delays. He argued that the OPC should be accessible to 
people who need it. 
b. Councilor Traverse acknowledged the urgency of establishing an OPC but expressed a different 
perspective on location, referring to examples in other cities. Further discussion clarified that 
accessibility near the central district was an important consideration.  
c. Councilor Traverse indicated that the revised resolution was expected to be discussed by City Council on 
October 26, 2026, with the intention of replacing the original version and determining the appropriate 
process and timeline for continued review. Refer to the video. 
7. Next Steps 
a. Councilor Sanchez Parkinson shared her interest in developing recommendations for a citywide youth 
strategy and potential investments, with the goal of returning to the committee around January. 
Reviewing of the revised Burlington Forward Resolution will continue. Refer to the video. 
8. Adjournment 
a. The meeting was adjourned at 7:39 pm.
